b.h2: Tell us what you need built.
b.lede: We reply within one business day with a technical read of the problem — not a service catalogue.
b.name: Name
b.ph: What exists today, what needs to exist, and what is in the way.
b.sent.p: We will read it properly and reply within one business day, at the email you left.
hero.h1: The team behind the packages you already run.
hero.lede: Aviary for NestJS and Agora for AdonisJS — 178 MIT packages on npm, pulled 207k times a month. Commercial support, custom adapters, and direct access to the engineers who wrote them.
o.agora: The same design, ported to AdonisJS — including a full OIDC identity provider and a payments layer with eighteen gateways behind a single contract.
o.aviary: Observability, durable workflows, governed AI agents and a metadata registry — the pieces a serious NestJS product needs and usually rewrites from scratch.
o.h2: Our engineering is public. Read it before you hire us.
o.lede: Each bar is a library family; its length is how many packages that family publishes. All on npm, all MIT, all in production.
p.h2: Four stages, and you always know which one you are in.
p.lede: None of them is optional and none of them happens quietly. You get each stage's artifact before the next one starts.
p.s1p: We read the system you already have — code, database, deploys, incidents. You get a map of what is blocking you and what is most expensive to leave alone.
p.s2p: We write down what gets built before building it. Decisions recorded with their reasoning attached, so a year from now it is still clear why the system works this way.
p.s3p: Continuous delivery, with tests on the path that can lose money. You follow it in a running environment, not in a slide deck.
p.s4p: Observability wired in from the first deploy. When something breaks at three in the morning, the answer is on a dashboard — not at the end of an investigation.
s.arch.p: One hard structural decision, a system that stopped scaling, a migration nobody wants to start.
s.h2: Three ways to work with us.
s.proj.p: From brief to deploy, with the whole team. You get the system running and code you can maintain without us.
s.sup.p: You already run Aviary or Agora in production. Commercial support from the people who wrote them.
st.lede: Not a list of everything we have touched. It is where we have a published library — which means we know how it behaves when it fails, not just what the docs say.
